articles.headline: Ethereum leads stablecoins with 54.1% share; its tokenized stock market hits $827M amid rapid growth.
articles.description: Ethereum remains the dominant blockchain for stablecoins, accounting for about 54.1% of all stablecoins issued, totaling around $162.5 billion out of a $300 billion market. Its tokenized stock market has grown 170% year-over-year to approximately $827 million, though it still represents a small fraction compared to stablecoins. While Ethereum leads in stablecoin issuance, BNB Chain leads in tokenized equities, with the overall tokenized stock market surpassing $3 billion. Investors are watching whether tokenized stocks might follow the growth trajectory of stablecoins in the coming years.

articles.headline: THORChain halts swaps after Ethereum glitch cau...
articles.description: THORChain paused most cross-chain swaps after an Ethereum reorganization led to a user being refunded twice for a 10 ETH deposit. This emergency halt affected all users on those bridges, extending beyond the single account involved. Chainalysis linked the disrupted route to North Korean hackers laundering stolen Binance funds, meaning the pause also delayed illicit activity. The incident highlights risks in cross-chain protocols and temporarily slowed a major laundering operation.

articles.headline: Bitcoin holds up better than Ethereum, XRP, and BNB after Binance hack triggers crypto market volatility.
articles.description: Following the Binance hack, Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and BNB all saw increased volatility with varying declines. Bitcoin showed resilience, dropping only 6.5% from its recent high and maintaining support around $76,000. BNB fell 14%, impacted by its Binance association but still stronger than Ethereum and XRP, which dropped 20.6% and 23% respectively, both falling below key support levels. The market now watches if these assets can regain lost ground amid ongoing uncertainty.
